bufferedWaitDelay.text: This command sets WaitDelay while its output goes to memory, here or in a caller it is returned to, so exec copies that output through a pipe of its own and Wait stops copying a fixed time after the process exits. A run slow to drain, or a descendant still holding the pipe, then fails with exec.ErrWaitDelay by chance, and the red lands on whoever runs next. Run it with Capture from `{{cure}}`, which reads each stream to its end with no timer, or, if the delay is meant, say why in a `// WaitDelay: <reason>` comment at the end of its line or directly above it.

bufferedWaitDelayWithoutReason.text: This WaitDelay on a buffered command is marked and gives no reason. Say why the delay is safe after `WaitDelay:`, such as the child starting no descendant, or reach for Capture from `{{cure}}` instead, because a marker with nothing after it tells the next reader nothing and excuses nothing.
